purpose: Bezlotoxumab is used to help prevent a Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection from coming back in adults who are already being treated for it with antibiotics. C. diff is a bacteria that causes serious diarrhea and gut problems. This medicine is especially helpful for people who are at high risk of getting C. diff again after their current infection is treated.
how_it_works: Bezlotoxumab is a special lab-made protein called a monoclonal antibody that targets and blocks a harmful toxin (called Toxin B) made by the C. diff bacteria. By neutralizing this toxin, it helps stop the bacteria from damaging the lining of your gut. Think of it like a shield that catches the toxin before it can cause harm and prevents the infection from returning.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, headache, fever, dizziness, and fatigue (feeling tired) are the most commonly reported side effects. Most of these are mild and short-lived.
warnings: This medication should be used with caution if you have a history of heart failure, as it may worsen heart conditions in some patients. It is given as a single IV infusion in a healthcare setting, so your team will monitor you during and after the infusion. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medications before receiving this treatment. It is not an antibiotic and should not be used alone to treat an active C. diff infection.
typical_dosing: Bezlotoxumab is given as a one-time intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein over 60 minutes. The standard dose is 10 mg per kilogram of your body weight. It is always given in a clinic or hospital setting alongside your antibiotic treatment for C. diff — you will not take this medication at home.
